newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks close lower, hit by interest rate woes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks close lower, hit by interest rate woes.

text.p: Wall Street stocks closed lower on Wednesday, as higher interest rates intensified pressure on equities.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 52 points to close unofficially at 6549, ending a brief streak in which the blue chips set record highs in two straight sessions despite weakness in the bond market.
Analysts said the declining bond market finally caught up to stocks on Wednesday.

"What's happened in the last few days is stocks have lost their cushion," said Douglas Cliggott, U.S. equity strategist at J.P. Morgan. "With bond yields backing up the way they have, I would characterize stocks as fully valued."

Concerns about interest rates, which resurfaced in force after a surprisingly strong National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) report last week, have intensified ahead of two key economic reports due later this week -- the producer price index on Thursday and monthly employment figures on Friday.
While stocks have shown a great deal of volatility this week, they have essentially run in place. The Dow's loss on Wednesday left it virtually unchanged from its opening on Monday.

"The market is waiting for some event to give it a catalyst," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "I think the best candidate will be the employment data on Friday, but it could come from the PPI."
A group of economists surveyed by Reuters expect, on average, an overall 0.3 percent rise in December producer prices.
The so-called "core" rate, which excludes the volatile food and energy components, is expected to show a 0.1 percent rise.
Both estimates were similar to November levels.

In a pattern becoming almost routine lately, the session was marked by a wave of program trades, seven on the day, according to Birinyi Associates. Five of the seven were sell programs. In all, program trading had a net negative impact of 106.69 points, the firm said.
Shares in major money center banks fared well on the session, despite the rise in interest rates.

Analysts said the gains by banks came amid expectations of strong earnings reports next week. Also, the banking industry got a boost when the Federal Reserve proposed removing many barriers to banks' activities in the securities industry.
Chase Manhattan Corp rose 7/8 to 87-5/8 and J.P. Morgan & Co Inc gained 1-1/8 to 99-3/8.
Templeton Russia Fund fell 1-1/8 to 23 after news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had been hospitalized after showing signs of pneumonia.

Loewen Group Inc fell 4-1/8 to 36-3/4 in NYSE activity after Service Corp International withdrew a $2.9 billion hostile offer for the funeral services company. Shares in Service Corp rose 1-3/4 to 29-3/8.

Shiva Corp plunged 15-5/8 to 19-1/4 in the first trading since the networking equipment maker warned that its fourth-quarter earnings would fall well short of consensus estimates. Several Wall Street firms downgraded the shares.
Netscape Communications Corp tumbled 10-7/8 to 47-7/8 after Deutsche Morgan Grenfell downgraded the shares to accumulate from buy.
The S&P 500 fell 4.82 to 748.41.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 7.38 to 1320.35.
Volume remained heavy, totalling 556.6 million shares on the NYSE, where declining issues edged out advancers 1280 to 1231.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
((Wall Street desk 212 859-1721))
